newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate rises 70 bps to 8.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate rises 70 bps to 8.4 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate rose 70 basis points to 8.4 percent on Friday amid stronger interbank borrowing on Zagreb's money market.
New demand pushed total trade up to 37.9 million kuna, against 65 million on the supply side.
Dealers said one larger loan, struck at 16 percent before a recent rate decline, was rolled over at 10 percent. This boosted the weighted call money rate to 9.7 from 8.0 percent.
Insurers' short-term rates were flat at seven percent.
Thursday's overnight settlements reached 53.5 million kuna banks with shortfalls borrowed 35 million and the rest was sold to two banks for maintaining their statutory reserves.

The central bank stayed out of the hard currency market. Its kuna midrates for Saturday and Monday eased to 5.3731 to the dollar while staying little changed at 3.5513 to the mark. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
